Option / tools: Copilot Studio agent + Power Automate flow
Primary purpose / workflow: SharePoint/OneDrive intake -> flow enumerates receipts -> OCR/AI extraction action or approved agent call -> structured output -> claims comparison -> exception queue.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Observed organizational blocker: cross-geography data movement is disabled and Copilot Studio generative functionality is not reliably usable; confirm exact affected features with admin.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Architecturally yes for a flow iterating 500 files, subject to quotas, connector access, reliable callable processing and retries. Not feasible with the affected agent in the present environment.
Input format / orientation handling: Input conversion still needed for unsupported formats (e.g. DOCX embedded photos and HEIC), skew/rotation and unreadable scans.
Structured information / claims matching: Potential to produce provider, member, service date, service description and paid amount; claim matching needs a separate validated rule layer.
Strengths: Microsoft ecosystem; file intake, audit trails, retries, structured outputs and human review can be orchestrated.
Key limitations / risks: Cross-geo setting blocks required agent features; DLP, agent invocation, execution time, credits/capacity, and data governance may block practical operation. Agent calls are not automatically equivalent to a full batch job.
Ongoing manual effort: Low for clean cases; higher for exceptions
Security / licensing / dependencies: Power Platform admin approval of geographic processing, relevant connectors and licenses; approved claims data path.
Recommended next step: Document as future-state option; request written IT confirmation of permitted region and whether all required agent/flow actions can be enabled.

Option / tools: Power Automate agent connectors / agent invocation actions
Primary purpose / workflow: Use approved connector/actions in an automated flow to call an agent per receipt and capture its JSON output.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Observed organizational blocker: relevant agent connectors are blocked by tenant/environment DLP policy; no short-term enablement expected per project discussion.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Technically possible if the action is supported, accessible and licensed; currently no reliable connector path to process 500 files.
Input format / orientation handling: Depends on the agent and input payload; may need file content conversion and size/format checks.
Structured information / claims matching: Could standardize receipt attributes; deterministic claims comparison still required.
Strengths: Centralized flow orchestration and good operational visibility if enabled.
Key limitations / risks: DLP enforcement prevents use; connector naming and exact supported call pattern should be verified with admin. Premium entitlements/capacity and throttling may apply.
Security / licensing / dependencies: DLP/Power Platform administrator decision; connector permissions, appropriate service connections and flow licensing.
Recommended next step: Keep as an explicit governance blocker; do not design the near-term solution around an exemption that has not been approved.

Option / tools: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat agent with SharePoint/OneDrive/other connectors
Primary purpose / workflow: Agent retrieves or interprets accessible documents when a user prompts it; possibly reference files from a connected source.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Interactive capability is available in principle; an approved unattended agent-invocation pathway has not been demonstrated in the current setup.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: No supported automatic 500-file scheduled invocation established for this chat agent in the current environment; document access through a connector is not the same as processing every file and exporting every result.
Input format / orientation handling: Connector availability and indexed file types vary; visual content in embedded images or unusual file formats may not be correctly extracted.
Structured information / claims matching: Useful for exploring schemas and manual interpretation, but reliable per-file JSON, evidence tracking and full claims matching require separate workflow/tooling.
Strengths: Reuses existing M365 experiences, permissions and user familiarity.
Key limitations / risks: Conversational, user-initiated interaction is difficult to scale; retrieval may skip documents, output may be non-repeatable, and large file collections may not be exhaustively processed.
Implementation effort (relative): Low for demo; high for true automation
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved tenant connectors, licensing and data permissions; a supported programmable processing interface would need verification.
Recommended next step: Use only for schema prototyping/spot checks. Do not present chat-agent connectors as an established batch-processing mechanism.

Option / tools: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat / manual receipt uploads
Primary purpose / workflow: Analyst uploads a limited batch of receipts or extracted text, asks Copilot to populate a predefined table and checks results.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Available as an interactive testing option; usable upload count and image support depend on license, chat surface, file size and tenant configuration; exact operational limit not yet verified.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Not an unattended 500-file pipeline. A person must split, upload, monitor, validate and consolidate batches.
Input format / orientation handling: PDF/Office support is documented for chat; verify image, DOCX-embedded-photo and HEIC behavior with representative files rather than assuming support.
Structured information / claims matching: Can suggest provider/member/service date/service type/paid amount for readable items; review every record and ask for source-page evidence.
Strengths: Fast to test with no engineering setup; good comparative benchmark for readable examples.
Key limitations / risks: Manual processing, context/output truncation, inconsistent structured results, ambiguous dates/amounts, hallucinated fields and potentially expensive review time.
Security / licensing / dependencies: M365 license/tenant file upload entitlements, privacy and acceptable file-upload location; do not assume unlimited uploads with premium licensing.
Near-term feasibility: Feasible for small samples, not bulk operations
Recommended next step: Keep as benchmark for 10-20 diverse receipts; record actual batch-size/format limitations and per-file operator time.

Option / tools: Existing Python: PDF text extraction + Tesseract OCR + Copilot spot checks
Primary purpose / workflow: Extract native text from digital PDFs; preprocess raster pages/images and run Tesseract; store OCR method, confidence, action flag and text in JSONL; manually test readable output in Copilot.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Prototype completed on 22 sample documents. 13/22 (59%) had sufficient readable information for comparison; 9/22 (41%) required reprocessing or human review. Not a verified accuracy score.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Yes, Python can loop through 500 files and generate a manifest/JSONL, but quality gates are required before automated matching.
Input format / orientation handling: Handles image/PDF OCR through preprocessing; DOCX embedded images require extraction/rendering; HEIC requires conversion; rotation/skew/perspective and multi-page handling need explicit testing.
Structured information / claims matching: Existing prototype extracts text, not guaranteed correct provider/member/date/service/amount fields. Copilot was generally able to identify fields in readable material.
Strengths: Working baseline, local operation possible, low incremental tooling cost, extraction metadata and human-review tagging already prototyped.
Key limitations / risks: 41% (9/22) low-readability sample cases; scanned/photo quality remains the bottleneck. OCR confidence is not calibrated field correctness; test sample small and may not represent actual files.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved local execution/storage and access controls for personal and claims data; Python dependencies, file-format conversion tools.
Recommended next step: Preserve as reference implementation. Add file inventory, orientation correction, DOCX image extraction, HEIC conversion, logging and labeled ground-truth evaluation.
Evidence / references: Internal 22-document prototype summary supplied in project note; no external source

Option / tools: Python pipeline: native text/OCR + rules + exception queue (without LLM)
Primary purpose / workflow: Batch inventory -> convert/extract by file type -> orientation and image cleanup -> PDF text/OCR -> regex/normalization for fields -> source citations -> exact/fuzzy claim comparison -> manual review.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Not fully implemented as an end-to-end pipeline; build on existing Python prototype with currently controlled infrastructure.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Yes. Python can independently ingest 500+ documents, checkpoint each file, retry failures and export CSV/JSONL; only confident matches proceed.
Input format / orientation handling: Add HEIC/HEIF conversion, DOCX image extraction, PDF page rendering, duplicate detection, auto-rotate, deskew and configurable fallbacks.
Structured information / claims matching: Best for predictable fields such as currency/date and reliable IDs; provider and service labels need curated mappings/approximate matching, with strict safeguards.
Strengths: Does not need an external generative-AI service; transparent matching, easy QA and auditable source snippets.
Key limitations / risks: Rules may fail across heterogeneous layouts, low OCR quality, handwritten content and subtle clinic-vs-practitioner naming. False positive claims matches are high risk.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved Python environment, local file access, review process, matching business rules and provider alias list.
Long-term feasibility: Medium-to-high for mixed-quality docs with human fallback
Recommended next step: Prioritize a no-agent end-to-end pilot; use conservative confidence thresholds, never silently auto-clear ambiguous claims.

Option / tools: Python OCR + locally hosted text-only LLM
Primary purpose / workflow: Use existing OCR text as input to an approved on-prem/local text LLM to map variable layouts to a strict JSON schema; enforce field validation, evidence and review.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Potential technical alternative; model host, compute, policy and access to local weights are not yet confirmed for this project.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Yes if a model endpoint or local Python runtime is approved and throughput can be managed; queue 500 files with batching, retries and output validation.
Input format / orientation handling: Still requires the same OCR and format normalization pipeline as Python. A text-only LLM cannot recover text that OCR failed to read.
Structured information / claims matching: Could improve field normalization across layouts and provider synonyms, but generated values must be tied to original OCR spans and validated against claims.
Strengths: Does not require Copilot Studio agent connectors if all inference runs on approved local infrastructure; reusable extraction schema.
Key limitations / risks: LLM may invent or swap dates/amounts or infer missing member names; slow inference, model-maintenance cost, privacy and audit burden; may offer little value if OCR is poor.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved model weights/license, hosting and compute (CPU/GPU), security review, deterministic JSON validation and no unapproved transfer of sensitive data.
Near-term feasibility: Conditional; needs approved host and benchmark
Recommended next step: Test text-only LLM on the same correctly OCRed 13 and the difficult 9 separately; compare against rules and do not confuse model interpretation with OCR recovery.
Evidence / references: Engineering proposal; validate local model governance and performance

Option / tools: Python + locally hosted vision-language/document AI model
Primary purpose / workflow: Render document pages or images and use a locally hosted multimodal OCR/document model; fall back to native PDF text, Tesseract or human review.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Exploratory; no approved specific vision-capable model, GPU capacity or deployment has been confirmed.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Possible in principle through an approved local API and job queue; throughput on 500 receipts depends on hardware, image size and model speed.
Input format / orientation handling: May cope better with some rotations/layouts, but HEIC/DOCX conversion, multi-page handling, image quality and resolution limits still apply.
Structured information / claims matching: Could output structured fields from images; must validate transcription, source regions and downstream matching separately.
Strengths: Potential to improve difficult photographed/layout-rich receipts beyond plain-text OCR.
Key limitations / risks: High compute and infrastructure complexity; model hallucination, poor small-text reading, unpredictable results and privacy/retention requirements; not guaranteed superior to Tesseract.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved multimodal model, VRAM/CPU resources, model licensing, secure endpoints, evaluation/monitoring and error controls.
Recommended next step: Test a small hard-case subset against existing OCR and human ground truth before considering production deployment.
Evidence / references: Engineering proposal; no vendor performance claim

Option / tools: Power Automate + AI Builder receipt processing / text recognition
Primary purpose / workflow: Automated file intake -> Apply to each -> AI Builder receipt or text recognition action -> format normalization -> claims matching -> review queue.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Microsoft-documented no-agent path; entitlement, admin permissions, AI Builder credits, data geography and organization DLP not yet checked.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Potentially yes within approved flow loops/capacity and model call quotas; 500 files need throughput, retry and cost testing.
Input format / orientation handling: Prebuilt receipt processing supports specified image/PDF formats; non-supported HEIC/DOCX need conversion. Separate text recognition model also exists.
Structured information / claims matching: Receipt model returns merchant, transaction date, items and total; health-claims fields like member identity, actual service date and practitioner may not map cleanly.
Strengths: Low-code integration with Power Automate; field confidence and source text available for review.
Key limitations / risks: May be blocked by permissions/DLP, have AI credit cost, need domain-specific fields and may mistake transaction date for service date. Generic retail receipts differ from benefit claim documents.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Confirm AI Builder capability and credits, supported region, allowed connector, sample-data authorization and availability of flow actions.
Recommended next step: Ask admin whether AI Builder actions work under current restrictions. If yes, run side-by-side test on 22 documents; retain only if it improves field-level accuracy.

Option / tools: Azure AI Document Intelligence (prebuilt receipt / Read / custom extraction)
Primary purpose / workflow: Approved Azure service receives supported document pages -> returns OCR/structured fields -> Python/Power Automate normalizes -> claims matching -> review queue.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Available as a Microsoft cloud service, but whether tenant has an approved resource, location, network route and budget is unverified.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Yes via Python SDK/REST or approved orchestration, with request rate, document/page size and pay-per-page cost to assess.
Input format / orientation handling: Read supports PDF, common images including HEIF and Office documents; model-specific support differs. Receipt prebuilt and custom models should be checked per file type; DOCX with embedded images may need conversion for receipt model.
Structured information / claims matching: Prebuilt receipts emphasize merchant/date/total; healthcare fields may need custom extraction and separate business-rule matching.
Strengths: Specialized OCR/document APIs with structured fields; scalable under Azure governance once approved.
Key limitations / risks: New subscription/resource approval and cost; document data handling/region, possible cloud processing prohibition; no guarantee that all receipt schemas work without custom training.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Azure approval, data-residency/security review, paid resource, identity/network access, model-selection and cost sign-off.
Long-term feasibility: High potential if allowed and validated
Recommended next step: Investigate only if organization allows approved Azure AI extraction; benchmark prebuilt and custom extraction on identical labeled samples.

Option / tools: Power Automate as file orchestrator + approved Python batch processor (no agent)
Primary purpose / workflow: Flow inventories files/creates work list in SharePoint; an approved scheduled Python process pulls available files and writes CSV/JSONL plus review status; optional flow notifies team.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Architecture proposal, not confirmed: ordinary SharePoint/OneDrive connectors and permitted local automation need validation. No Copilot Studio dependency.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Yes if an approved transfer/trigger bridge exists; the Python side can process 500 while Power Automate manages intake/status; otherwise run Python alone.
Input format / orientation handling: All problematic formats handled at Python layer using converter/extractor plugins.
Structured information / claims matching: Leverages Python extraction of fields and offline matching rules; human review remains for unreliable cases.
Strengths: Clean separation of file logistics and extraction; avoids blocked generative agent connector when ordinary connectors are approved.
Key limitations / risks: Ordinary connectors may also be blocked; triggers/service accounts, file permissions, scheduling and failure reconciliation must be designed.
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved SharePoint/OneDrive access, service identity, task scheduler/server or approved webhook, operational ownership.
Near-term feasibility: Conditional; no-agent Python alone is fallback
Long-term feasibility: High if standard flow and Python host are approved
Recommended next step: Check whether ordinary SharePoint flow steps are allowed. If not, run Python batch directly on approved secure file share and generate audit CSV.

Option / tools: Human reviewer + controlled spreadsheet (baseline or exception handling)
Primary purpose / workflow: An analyst examines original receipts, records fields and matches to claims; OCR drafts may prefill but reviewer validates against document and claim record.
Current organizational status (Nov 2026): Operationally possible subject to approved access; actual existing staff capacity and process time not measured.
Can handle ~500 receipts unattended?: Yes as a project of 500 individual reviews, but not automated; turnaround scales with staffing and document complexity.
Input format / orientation handling: Can handle unusual, rotated, damaged or embedded formats when humans can view them; unreadable originals may require resubmission.
Structured information / claims matching: High contextual judgment for clinic vs provider and ambiguous amounts; double-check sensitive decisions.
Strengths: Provides ground-truth labels, strong fallback and reference cost for automation ROI.
Key limitations / risks: High labor and inconsistency risk, limited repeatability, audit burden, reviewer fatigue; manual may still fail on unreadable source.
Implementation effort (relative): Low tooling effort; high operational effort
Security / licensing / dependencies: Approved access, reviewer instructions, QA sampling, protected storage and confidentiality controls.
Long-term feasibility: Essential as exception queue / validation baseline
Recommended next step: Time 20-30 receipts per complexity tier to estimate labor and build a labeled evaluation set; establish escalation/resubmission process.
